decision_reason: The observed eight-hour display offset is real and non-critical, but its cause is the platform-wide database-session, storage, and timezone-less API contract. A release-only correction would create inconsistent timestamp semantics across modules.

causal_assessment.hypothesis: MySQL CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is evaluated in the UTC container session while JDBC and JSON expose timezone-less LocalDateTime values interpreted as Shanghai wall time.
supporting_evidence: The binding operation performed around 16:50 displayed as 08:50:52.
application-local.yml declares serverTimezone=Asia/Shanghai, but there is no central forceConnectionTimeZoneToSession or offset-bearing API contract.
Multiple existing platform migrations and services use CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and LocalDateTime, so the causal surface is not release-specific.
causal_assessment.falsifier: A controlled connection showing MySQL session time_zone already set to Asia/Shanghai while the same stored instant and API serialization still reproduce the offset.

invariants: Do not reinterpret existing persisted DATETIME values without a migration policy.
Preserve workflow binding and audit data already verified.
control_action.impact_limit: No product-code action in REQ-032; future correction must cover representative platform modules and existing data semantics.
correction_check: Define whether stored timestamps are UTC instants or Asia/Shanghai wall time.
Configure the database session and JSON contract consistently.
Verify binding history plus representative workflow, system, and form-metadata timestamps around a known instant.
Document compatibility treatment for existing DATETIME values.

residual_risk: Audit times can display approximately eight hours behind local business time until the platform contract is normalized.
A future central fix must account for existing rows to avoid double-shifting historical data.
